Surah al-Shura (Surah 42)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Fasl (separate letters): Ha Mim, [and] 'Ayn Sin Qaf, written differently from Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad [Maryam: 1], in order to combine them with their counterparts (akhawat), and because this is two verses, whereas "Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad" is one verse.

Surah al-Shura (Surah 42)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Fasl (separate letters): Ha Mim, [and] 'Ayn Sin Qaf, written differently from Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad [Maryam: 1], in order to combine them with their counterparts (akhawat), and because this is two verses, whereas "Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad" is one verse.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 3:

﴿Thus does He reveal to you﴾, that is: like that revelation, or like that Book, He reveals to you,

﴿and to those before you﴾, and to the messengers before you,

﴿Allah﴾. That is to say: what this surah contains of meanings, Allah has revealed to you the like of it in other surahs, and revealed it to those before you, meaning to His messengers. The meaning is that Allah repeated these meanings in the Qur'an and in all the heavenly Books, because of the eloquent admonition in them and the great kindness to His servants. And from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "There was no prophet who possessed a Book except that he was revealed [the letters] Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf." The verb is "yuha" (revealed) with a fatha on the ha, [this is the reading of] Makki. On this reading, the subject of the passive verb "yuha" is the name of Allah, as if a questioner had asked, "Who is the one who reveals?" and it was answered, "Allah."

﴿the Mighty﴾, the Overpowering by His dominion,

﴿the Wise﴾, the One who is correct in His action and His speech.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: ownership (mulkan), and possession (milkan).

﴿And He is the Most High﴾: in His affair (sha'nuhu).

﴿The Most Great﴾: in His proof (burhanuhu).

(p. 245) ﴿*Takādu*, the heavens are almost splitting﴾, read with the *yā'* (*yakādu*) by Nāfi' and 'Alī,

﴿*yatafaṭṭarna* min fawqihinna﴾, meaning *yatashaqqaqna* (they split), read *yanfaṭirna* by Baṣrī (Abū 'Amr) and Abū Bakr. Its meaning is: they almost split apart from the exaltedness of Allah's majesty and greatness. This is supported by its coming after His saying "the Most High, the Great." It was also said that it refers to their attributing a son to Him, as in His saying, ﴿The heavens almost split apart from it﴾ [Maryam: 90]. As for "from above them," it means that the splitting begins from their upper side. The analogy (*qiyās*) would have been to say *yanfaṭirna min taḥtihinna* (from beneath them), from the direction from which the word of disbelief came, since it came from those who are beneath the heavens. But this was exaggerated, so the effect was attributed to the upper direction, as if it were said: they almost split from the direction above them, leaving aside the direction beneath them. It was also said that "from above them" means from above the earth, so the pronoun refers to the earth, since it carries the sense of "the earths." It was also said that they split because of the great number of angels upon the heavens. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The sky has creaked, and it has every right to creak. There is not a space the size of a foot in it except that an angel is standing there, or bowing, or prostrating."

﴿And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord﴾, in submission to what they see of His greatness,

﴿and seek forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, meaning for the believers among them, as in His saying, ﴿and they seek forgiveness for those who believe﴾ [Ghāfir: 7], out of fear for them of His punishment. Or they affirm Allah's oneness and declare Him far above what is not permissible for Him of attributes, praising Him for what He has bestowed upon them of His kindnesses, marvelling at what they see of their exposure to the wrath of Allah (Exalted is He). And they seek forgiveness for the believing people of the earth, who have disavowed that word. Or they ask their Lord to show forbearance toward the people of the earth and not hasten punishment upon them.

﴿Surely Allah, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, toward them.

Those who take protectors besides Him - ﴿Allah is Watcher over them﴾; that is, He made for Him partners and equals.

﴿Allah is Watcher over them﴾, observing over their statements and their deeds, nothing of them escapes Him, so He will recompense them for them.

﴿And you are not﴾, O Muhammad,

﴿a guardian over them﴾, one entrusted over them, nor one to whom their affair has been delegated; you are only a warner.

(p-246) ﴿Wa-kadhalika﴾ (And thus, likewise, in the same manner), ﴿awhaynā ilayka﴾ (We have revealed to you). "Dhalika" (that) is a reference to the meaning of the verse before it, namely that Allah is the Watcher over them, not you; rather, you are a warner. This is because Allah repeated this meaning in His Book. So the kaf (ka) is the direct object (maf'ul bihi) of awhaynā.

﴿Qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan﴾ (an Arabic Qur'an) is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) from the direct object, meaning: We have revealed to you, and it is a clear Arabic Qur'an.

﴿Li-tundhira umma l-qurā﴾ (that you may warn the Mother of Cities), i.e., Mecca, because the earth was spread out from beneath it, or because it is the most noble of places. The intended meaning is the people of Umm al-Qura.

﴿Wa-man ḥawlahā﴾ (and those around it), from among the Arabs.

﴿Wa-tundhira yawma l-jamʿ﴾ (and that you may warn of the Day of Assembly), i.e., the Day of Resurrection, because all creatures will be gathered on it.

﴿Lā rayba fīh﴾ (there is no doubt in it) is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ) with no grammatical place (lā maḥall lahu). It is said: "andhartuhu kadhā" (I warned him of such-and-such) and "andhartuhu bi-kadhā" (I warned him with such-and-such). ﴿Li-tundhira umma l-qurā﴾ has been made transitive to the first object, and "tundhira yawma l-jamʿ" to the second object.

﴿Farīqun fī l-jannati wa-farīqun fī l-saʿīr﴾ (a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze), i.e., from among them is a party in the Garden, and from among them is a party in the Blaze. The pronoun refers to the two groups together, because the meaning is "the Day of the gathering of creatures."

"And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community" — that is, all of them believers.

"But He admits whom He wills into His mercy" — that is, He honours whom He wills with Islam.

"And the wrongdoers" — the disbelievers —

"they have no protector" — no intercessor —

"nor any helper" — no one to repel (punishment).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 9:

﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him? But God, He is the Protector (al-Wali)﴾. The fa' (the particle of consequence, fa') here is the answer to an implied conditional clause (shart muqaddar), as if it were said, after the denial of every protector other than Him: "If they mean protectors in truth, then God is the Protector in truth, and He is the one who must be taken as protector alone, and there is no protector besides Him."

﴿And He is the One who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Powerful﴾. So He is the one worthy of being taken as protector, not one who has no power over anything.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 10:

﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment rests with Allah.﴾ This is the report of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the believers, meaning: whatever the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists opposed you in, so that you and they differed over it, of the matters of the religion,

﴿Its judgment﴾, meaning: the judgment concerning that matter of difference, is entrusted ﴿to Allah﴾, and it consists of rewarding those among the believers who are right in it and punishing the people of falsehood.

﴿That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied﴾, the Judge between you (p-247). In it is a refutation of the plotting of the enemies of the religion.

﴿And to Him I turn in repentance﴾, meaning I return to Him for protection from their evil. It has also been said: whatever disagreement has arisen among you concerning matters of knowledge that are not connected to your obligations, and for which you have no path to knowing, then say, "Allah knows best," as with the knowledge of the soul (rūḥ) and other such things.

**﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾**: its being in the nominative (*irtifa'uhu*) is because it is one of the predicates of "*dhalikum*" (that is), or the predicate of an omitted subject.

**﴿He made for you spouses from yourselves﴾**: He created for you, from your own kind, among mankind, spouses.

**﴿spouses, and of the livestock spouses﴾**: meaning, He also created for the livestock spouses from their own kind.

**﴿multiplies you﴾**: He makes you numerous. It is said: "Allah *dhara'a* the creation," meaning He spread them abroad and increased them.

**﴿in it﴾**: in this arrangement, which is that He made mankind and the livestock into pairs, so that between their males and females there is procreation and reproduction. The preposition "*fihi*" (in it) was chosen over "*bihi*" (by it), because He made this arrangement like the source and the mine for the spreading and multiplying. The pronoun in "*yadhra'ukum*" refers to the addressees and to the livestock, with the rational addressees given precedence over the non-rational absent beings.

**﴿Nothing is like Him﴾**: It is said that the word of comparison was repeated to emphasise the negation of likeness, and its underlying form is "*laysa mithluhu shay'*" (nothing is like His like). It is also said that "*mithl*" (like) is superfluous, and its underlying form is "*laysa kahuwa shay'*" (nothing is like Him), as in His saying: ﴿*If they believe in the like of what you have believed in*﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:137]. This is because the intended meaning is the negation of likeness; and if the particle *ka* (like) or the word *mithl* is not taken as superfluous, it would imply the affirmation of a like. It is also said that the intended meaning is "*laysa kadhatihi shay'*" (nothing is like His essence), because they say, "*Mithluka la yabkhalu*" (One like you does not act stingily), meaning by it the negation of stinginess from your essence. They intend by this an emphasis through the use of *kināya* (metonymy, allusive expression), because when they negate it from someone who fills his place, they have negated it from him. When it is known that this is from the category of *kināya*, there is no difference between his saying "*Nothing is like Allah*" and his saying "*Nothing is like His likeness*," except what the *kināya* gives of its benefit. The two expressions are as if they were alternative phrasings of one meaning, namely the negation of similarity from His essence. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿*rather, both His hands are outstretched*﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:64]. Its meaning is: rather, He is generous, without imagining a hand or an outstretching of it, because it has come to be an expression for generosity, to the extent that they have used it of one who has no hand. Likewise this is used of one who has a like, and of one who has no like.

**﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾**: of all things that are heard, without an ear.

**﴿the All-Seeing﴾**: of all things that are seen, without a pupil. It seems that He mentioned these two so that it would not be imagined that He has no attributes, just as He has no like.

(p-٢٤٨)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 12:

﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, which has passed in "al-Zumar" (Surah 39).

﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾, i.e., He constricts.

﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾

﴿شَرَعَ﴾ means بَيَّنَ (clarified) and أظْهَرَ (made manifest).

﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾. That is: He has ordained for you of religion the religion of Noah, of Muhammad (ﷺ), and of the prophets between them, upon them be peace. Then He explained the ordained matter in which these eminent messengers shared, by His saying: ﴿that you should establish the religion﴾. What is meant is the establishment of the religion of Islam, which is the affirmation of God's oneness (tawhid), obedience to Him, belief in His messengers and His books, in the Day of Recompense, and all that by which a person becomes a Muslim through establishing it. It does not mean the sharia (law), for these differ, as God says: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a way﴾ [al-Ma'ida 5:48].

The position (mahall) of ﴿an aqimu﴾ (that you establish) is accusative in i'rab (grammatical analysis, nasb), as a badal (substitute, apposition) for the object of ﴿shara'a﴾ (ordained) and what is conjoined to it; or nominative (raf'), by way of istinaf (resumption of a new sentence), as if it were said: "What is that ordained matter?" and it was answered: "It is the establishment of the religion."

﴿And do not be divided therein﴾: do not differ concerning the religion. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Do not be divided, for unity is mercy and division is punishment."

﴿It is hard upon the polytheists﴾: it is great upon them and burdensome for them.

﴿That to which you call them﴾: namely the establishment of the religion of God and tawhid.

﴿God chooses﴾: He draws to Himself and gathers.

﴿to Himself﴾: to the religion, through success (tawfiq) and guidance (taysid).

﴿whomever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾: whoever turns in submission to His obedience.

﴿And they did not become divided﴾, i.e., the People of the Book, after their prophets,

﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾, except after they had come to know that division is misguidance and a matter threatened against by the tongues of the prophets, upon them be peace,

﴿out of envy among themselves﴾, out of jealousy and a desire for leadership and superiority, ﴿without (p-249) right﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term﴾, and that word is: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾, they would have been destroyed when they committed (the sin), because of the enormity of what they committed.

﴿And indeed those who were given the Book after them﴾, they are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,

﴿are in doubt concerning it﴾, concerning their Book, not believing in it with true belief,

﴿disquieting﴾, causing (them) to enter into suspicion. It was also said: "And the People of the Book did not become divided except after knowledge of the sending of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had come to them," like His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿And those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 4]. ﴿And indeed those who were given the Book after them﴾ are the polytheists, who were given the Qur'an after the People of the Book had been given the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿فَلِذَلِكَ﴾: that is, because of that division, and because of what arose from it, namely the splitting of unbelief into many branches.

﴿فادْعُ﴾: invite (them) to unity and harmony upon the upright (ḥanīfiyya) religion (milla), which is firm.

﴿واسْتَقِمْ﴾: remain steadfast upon it, and upon calling others to it.

﴿كَما أُمِرْتَ﴾: as you have been commanded, as Allah has commanded you.

﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أهْواءَهُمْ﴾: and do not follow their desires, which are divergent and false.

﴿وَقُلْ آمَنتُ بِما أنْـزَلَ اللهُ مِن كِتابٍ﴾: and say, "I believe in whatever Scripture Allah has sent down." That is, any Scripture whose descent from Allah (Exalted) is sound. It means belief in all the revealed Books, because those who divided (their religion) believed in some and disbelieved in others, as in His saying: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others"﴾ [al-Nisa: 150], up to His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa: 151].

﴿وَأُمِرْتُ لأعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ﴾: "And I have been commanded to be just among you" in judgment, when you dispute and bring your disputes before me.

﴿اللهُ رَبُّنا ورَبُّكُمْ﴾: Allah is our Lord and your Lord; that is, we are all His servants.

﴿لَنا أعْمالُنا ولَكم أعْمالُكُمْ﴾: "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds." This is like His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun: 6]. It may also mean: we shall not be held accountable for your deeds, and you shall not be held accountable for ours.

﴿لا حُجَّةَ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَكُمُ﴾: "There is no argument between us and you." That is, there is no contention, because the truth has become manifest and you have been overcome by it, so there is no need for disputation. It may also mean that no proofs are to be presented between us, since two parties disputing each present their own argument.

﴿اللهُ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنا﴾: Allah will gather us together on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿وَإلَيْهِ المَصِيرُ﴾: "And to Him is the final return," the place of return, for the decisive judgment. So He will judge between us and take retribution on our behalf against you.

(p-250) ﴿And those who argue about God﴾ — they dispute concerning His religion,

﴿after it has been responded to﴾ — people had responded to it and entered Islam, so that [the disputants] might turn them back to the religion of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), like His saying: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109]. The Jews and the Christians used to say to the believers: "Our Book is before your Book, and our Prophet is before your Prophet, so we are better than you and more entitled to the truth." It was also said: "after it has been responded to" means after Muhammad ﷺ's supplication against the polytheists on the day of "Badr" had been answered.

﴿Their argument is futile﴾ — false, and He called it an argument even though it is a mere dubious point (shubhah), because of their claim that it is an argument.

﴿With their Lord, and upon them is wrath﴾ — because of their disbelief.

﴿And for them is a severe punishment﴾ — in the Hereafter.

Allah is the One who sent down the Book (أي: جنس الكتاب), meaning the category of the Book,

with the truth (بالحق), meaning with sincerity, or accompanied by it,

and the Balance (والميزان), meaning justice and equity. The meaning of the sending down of justice is that it was sent down in the revealed Books. It was also said that the Balance itself (عين الميزان) is meant: He sent it down in the time of Nuh, upon him be peace.

﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ That is: perhaps the Hour is near to you, while you do not know. What is intended is the coming of the Hour, and the Hour is interpreted as the Resurrection. The reason for the connection between the nearness of the Hour and the sending down of the Books and the Balance is that the Hour is the Day of Reckoning, and the setting up of the scales with justice. So it is as if it were said: "Allah has commanded you with justice and equity, and with acting by the laws, so act by the Book and by justice before the Day of your reckoning and the weighing of your deeds surprises you."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 18:

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it,﴾ in mockery.

﴿And those who believe are fearful of it,﴾ apprehensive,

﴿and know that it is the truth,﴾ that which will certainly occur,

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far-off error.﴾ The mira' (mira'ah, contention, persistent wrangling) is al-mulajjah (obstinate insistence), because each of the two parties draws out (yamri) what is in the possession of his companion. ﴿In far-off error﴾ means far from the truth, because the establishment of the Hour is not improbable given the power of Allah (exalted is He), and the Book and the Sunnah have indicated its occurrence, while the intellects bear witness that there must be an abode of recompense.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 19:

(p-251) ﴿Allah is Latif (Subtly Kind) to His servants﴾: in conveying benefits and averting affliction, by means whose perception is subtle. He is Barr (the Benevolent), of complete benevolence toward them, whose benevolence has reached all of them. It has also been said: He is the one whose knowledge penetrates hidden matters, and whose forbearance is great toward transgressions; or the one who spreads out virtues and conceals faults; or who pardons the one who slips; or who gives the servant beyond sufficiency and imposes on him obedience within his capacity. And from al-Junayd: "He was subtly kind to His friends, so they knew Him; and had He been subtly kind to His enemies, they would not have denied Him."

﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾: that is, He expands the provision of whomever He wills, when He knows the benefit for him in it. In a hadith: "Indeed, among My believing servants is one whose faith is not set right except by wealth; were I to make him poor, that would corrupt him. And among My believing servants is one whose faith is not set right except by poverty; were I to make him rich, that would corrupt him."

﴿And He is the Strong﴾, the one of overpowering power, who prevails over everything;

﴿the Mighty﴾, the Invincible, who cannot be overcome.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 42, verse 20:

﴿Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter﴾: he called what the doer does, by which he seeks benefit, "tillage" (*ḥarth*), figuratively (*majāz*, a figurative usage),

﴿We increase for him in his tillage﴾: by granting success in his deed, or by multiplying his good works, or by his attaining both this world and the Hereafter through it.

﴿And whoever desires the tillage of this world﴾: i.e., whoever's deed is for this world and who does not believe in the Hereafter,

﴿We give him of it﴾: i.e., some of it, because "مِن" (*min*) is for partition (*li'l-tab'īḍ*), and it is his provision that has been apportioned for him, not what he desires and seeks,

﴿and he has no share in the Hereafter﴾: he has no share at all in the Hereafter, while he has a share in this world. It is not mentioned concerning the doer of the Hereafter that his apportioned provision reaches him, out of disregard for that in comparison with what he is aiming at, namely the purification of his deed and his triumph in the return.

﴿Or do they have partners﴾. It is said: this is the disjunctive ﴿am﴾ (*am al-munqati'ah*), and its implied sense is: "Rather, do they have partners?!" It is also said: it is the ﴿am﴾ equivalent to the interrogative alif (*alif al-istifham*). The speech contains an implied element, whose sense is: "Will they accept what Allah has prescribed of religion, or do they have deities ﴿who have ordained for them in religion what Allah has not permitted﴾?!" That is, He did not command it.

﴿And were it not for the word of decision﴾, that is, the prior decree to postpone the recompense, that is, were it not for the promise that the decision would take place on the Day of Resurrection,

﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ [Ash-Shura: 14], between the disbelievers and the believers. Or: the punishment would have been hastened upon them.

﴿Indeed the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment﴾. Indeed the polytheists will have a painful punishment in the Hereafter, even if it is deferred from them in the abode of this world.

(p-252)

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 42, verse 22:**

﴿You will see the wrongdoers﴾: the polytheists (al-mushrikin), in the Hereafter,

﴿fearful﴾: frightened,

﴿of what they have earned﴾: of the recompense for their disbelief,

﴿and it will certainly befall them﴾: it will surely descend upon them, without doubt, whether they feared it or not.

﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the meadows of the gardens﴾: it is as if the meadow of the believer's garden is the most pleasant and the most delightful spot in it.

﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾: "'inda" (ʿinda, "with") is in the accusative case governed by the adverbial complement (ẓarf, an accusative of place or time), not by "yashaʾūna" (they wish).

﴿That is the great bounty﴾: in return for the small deed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 23:

﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 52], i.e., the great favour.

﴿الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللهُ﴾. "يُبَشِّرُ" (yubashshiru, with the doubled shin, "gives good news") is read by Makki, Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and ʿAlī.

﴿عِبادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصالِحاتِ﴾. The meaning is: "with it, His servants who believed." The preposition (al-jarr, "the governing preposition") has been omitted, as in His saying: ﴿And Musa chose from his people﴾ [Al-Araf: 155]. Then the returning pronoun referring back to the relative pronoun (al-ism al-mawsul) has been omitted, as in His saying: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ [Al-Furqan: 41]. When the polytheists said, "Does he seek a reward for conveying the message?", the verse was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾, referring to the conveying,

﴿except the affection (al-mawaddah) among kinsfolk (fi al-qurba)﴾. The phrase "illā al-mawaddah" may be a contiguous exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil, an exception of the same kind as what precedes it), meaning: "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except this: that you show affection to the people of my kinship." It may also be a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ, an exception of a different kind), meaning: "I do not ask you for any reward at all, but I ask you to show affection to my relatives, who are your relatives too, and not to harm them." The text does not say "illā mawaddata al-qurbā" or "al-mawaddata lil-qurbā", because they (the relatives) have been made the place of affection and its abode, as when you say: "I have affection for the family of so-and-so, and I have deep love for them", meaning: "I love them, and they are the place and locus of my love." The word "fī" is not a complement of "al-mawaddah" in the way that "lām" would be: if you say "illā al-mawaddata lil-qurbā", the phrase is connected to a deleted element, in the way that an adverbial of place (al-ẓarf) is connected to its verb, as in your saying: "the money is in the bag." Its estimated meaning is: "except affection that is established and firmly rooted among the kinsfolk." "Al-qurbā" is a verbal noun (maṣdar), like "al-zulfā" and "al-bushrā", meaning "kinship," and the intended sense is "among the people of kinship."

It is related that when the verse was revealed, it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are these relatives of yours whose affection has become obligatory upon us?" He said: "ʿAlī, Fatimah, and their two sons, may Allah be pleased with them." It was also said that its meaning is: "except that you show affection to me because of my kinship among you, and do not harm me or incite against me," since there was no branch of Quraysh with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not have kinship.

It was also said that "al-qurbā" means "seeking nearness to Allah (Exalted)," i.e., "except that you love Allah and His Messenger through your drawing near to Him by obedience and righteous deeds."

﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾, i.e., acquires an act of obedience. According to al-Suddi, it is affection for the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and his affection for them. The apparent sense is general, covering any good deed, but it primarily includes affection, because it is mentioned immediately after the mention of affection among kinsfolk.

﴿We shall increase for him therein good (ḥusnan)﴾, i.e., We shall multiply it, as in His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245]. It is also read "ḥusnā", which is a verbal noun like "al-bushrā". The pronoun refers either to the good deed or to Paradise.

﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ to whoever sins, by His bounty,

﴿Appreciative﴾ to whoever obeys, by His grace. It was also said: He accepts repentance and inspires it. It was also said: "al-Shakūr," as an attribute of Allah (Exalted), means that He takes account of obedience, fully rewards it, and bestows His favour upon the one who is rewarded.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 24:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ "Am" (or) is disjunctive (munqati'a), and the meaning of the interrogative hamza in it is rebuke (tawbikh), as if it were said: "Can they bring themselves to attribute the like of this to fabrication, and then to fabrication against Allah, which is the greatest of fabrications and the most abominable of them?!"

﴿So if Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾. Mujahid said: that is, He would bind your heart with patience in the face of their harm and of their saying, "He has invented a lie against Allah," so that no hardship would enter it because of their denial.

﴿And Allah will efface falsehood﴾, that is, shirk. This is a new independent sentence (kalam mubtada'), not conjoined to "yakhtim" (will seal), because the effacing of falsehood is not dependent on the condition; rather it is an unconditional promise. The evidence for this is the repetition of the name of Allah (Exalted), and the nominative case of ﴿wayuhiqqu﴾ (and He establishes). The waw was dropped in the script, as it was dropped in ﴿wayad'u al-insanu bil-sharri du'a'ahu bil-khayr﴾ [al-Isra: 11] and ﴿sanad'u al-zabaniyah﴾ [al-Alaq: 18], although it is recorded in the Mushaf of Nafi'.

﴿And He establishes the truth﴾, and makes Islam manifest and firm.

﴿by His words﴾ (p-254) by what He sent down of His Book upon the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ). Allah has done that: He effaced their falsehood and manifested Islam.

﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, that is, Knowing of what is in your breast and their breasts, and He will recompense accordingly.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 25:

﴿He it is who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. It is said: "I accepted (qabiltu) the thing from him," when I took it from him and made it the starting point of my acceptance. It is also said: "I accepted it from him (qabiltuhu 'anhu)," meaning: I removed it from him and separated it from him. As for "tawbah" (repentance, lit. returning), it is that one turns back from what is ugly and from neglecting an obligation, by regret over both and resolve not to return to them. If it involves a right of a servant, there is no escape from freeing oneself of it by its proper means. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is a term that applies to six meanings: for the past sins, regret; for neglecting the obligations, making them up; restoring the wrongs (to their owners); melting the self in obedience just as you had nurtured it in disobedience; making the self taste the bitterness of obedience just as you had made it taste the sweetness of disobedience; and weeping in place of every laugh you have laughed." And from al-Suddi: "It is the sincere resolve to abandon sins, and turning in the heart to the Knower of the unseen." And from others: it is that one does not find the sweetness of the sin in the heart when remembering it. And from Sahl: "It is the transition from blameworthy states to praiseworthy states." And from al-Junayd: "It is turning away from everything other than Allah,"

﴿and pardons the bad deeds﴾, which are what is below shirk; He pardons whom He wills without repentance,

﴿and He knows what you do﴾, with the letter ta' (tafalun, "you do"), according to all the Kufans except Abu Bakr, meaning: of repentance and disobedience. There is no pause upon it, because of its conjunction with what precedes it and the continuity of meaning.

﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty.﴾ That is: when they call upon Him, He answers their supplication, gives them what they asked for, and adds to them beyond what they requested. "Istajaba" (responded) and "ajaba" (answered) have the same meaning, and the sin (s) in such a form serves to emphasise the verb, as when you say "ta'azzama" (became great) and "asta'zama" (considered something great). The implied sense is: "And Allah answers those who believe." It has also been said that the meaning is: "and He responds to those who believe," with the preposition lam (li) omitted. He bestows favour upon them by accepting their repentance when they repent, pardoning their misdeeds, answering them when they call upon Him, and increasing them beyond what they asked of Him. It is related from Ibrahim ibn Adham that he was asked: "What is the matter with us? We call upon Him, yet we are not answered?" He said: "Because He has called you, and you did not respond to Him."

﴿As for the disbelievers, they will have a severe punishment﴾, in the Hereafter.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 42, verse 27:**

﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants﴾, i.e., if He made them all rich,

﴿they would surely transgress in the earth﴾. It is from "al-baghy", which means oppression, i.e., "one of them would oppress the other, and the other would oppress him," because wealth is a cause of insolence and arrogance (mabtaratun, ma'shara), and the states of Qarun and Pharaoh are sufficient as a lesson. Or it is from "al-baghy", which means pride, i.e., they would become arrogant in the earth.

﴿But He sends down﴾ — with the lightened reading (takhfif), recited by Makki and Abu 'Amr —

﴿in a measure as He wills﴾: with a determination. It is said: "qaddarahu, qadran, and qadaran" (he measured it out).

﴿Indeed He is Aware of His servants, Seeing﴾: He knows their conditions, so He determines for them what His wisdom requires. Thus He makes some poor and some rich, withholds and gives, restricts and expands. If He had made them all rich, they would transgress; if He had made them all poor, they would perish. What you see of expansion upon those who transgress, and of transgression without expansion, is rare. There is no doubt that transgression accompanied by poverty is less, and accompanied by expansion is more numerous and more prevalent.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 28:

﴿And He it is who sends down the rain﴾ — with the doubled consonant (tashdid) — "Madani, Shami and ʿAsim" (the readers of Medina, Syria and ʿAsim),

﴿after they have despaired﴾. It was also read: "qanitu" (with the vowel of the second radical differing),

﴿and spreads His mercy﴾, meaning: the blessings of the rain, its benefits, and the fertility that results from it. It was said to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "The drought has become severe and the people have despaired." He said: "Then they have been given rain." He meant this verse, or he meant His mercy in everything.

﴿And He is the Walī﴾, who takes charge of His servants with His kindness,

﴿the Ḥamīd﴾, the One praised for that, whom the people of His obedience praise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 29:

﴿And among His signs﴾, i.e., the indications of His power,

﴿is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, despite their immensity,

﴿and what He has scattered﴾, i.e., dispersed, and "what" (mā) may be in the nominative or the genitive case, taking it as agreeing with the thing it is attached to, or with the thing to which it is attached,

﴿in them﴾, i.e., in the heavens and the earth,

﴿of living creatures﴾. Living creatures (dawābb, sing. dābba) are found on the earth alone, but it is permissible to attribute a thing to the whole of what is mentioned even if it is associated with only part of it, as one says, "The Banū Tamīm have among them a skilled poet," when he is in fact from one of their clans (afkhādh). And from this is His (exalted) saying: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 22], whereas they come forth only from the salt water. It is not far-fetched that He creates in the heavens living beings that walk in them as human beings walk on the earth, or that the angels have a walking together with their flying, so they are described as crawling, just as human beings are described with it.

﴿And He is able to gather them﴾, on the Day of Resurrection,

﴿whenever He wills﴾. "Idhā" (whenever) may be followed by the present tense, just as it is followed by the past tense. God (exalted) said: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 30:

﴿And whatever affliction befalls you﴾ — i.e., distress, pain, and something disliked;

﴿it is because of what your hands have earned﴾ — i.e., because of a sin you have committed, as a punishment for it. The reading "bi-mā kasabat" without the fā' (ف) is that of Madinan and Syrian readers, on the basis that "mā" is a subject (mubtada'), and "bi-mā kasabat" is its predicate, without implying the meaning of a condition (sharṭ). Whoever affirms the fā' (فَ) does so on the basis of implying the meaning of a condition (sharṭ).

Those who hold the doctrine of metempsychosis (tanāsukh) cling to this verse and say: "If children had no state in which they were before this state, they would not suffer." We say: the verse is specific to those who are legally responsible (mukallafūn), by the context (sibāq) and the wider context (siyāq), which is: ﴿and He pardons much﴾, i.e., of the sins, so He does not punish for it; or "of much" of the people, so He does not deal with them by punishment.

Ibn 'Aṭā' said: "Whoever does not know that what reaches him of trials and calamities is due to his own earning, and that what his Master has pardoned is greater, has little regard for the goodness of his Lord toward him."

Muḥammad ibn Ḥāmid said: "The servant is constantly engaged in offenses at every moment, and his offenses in obedience are greater than his offenses in disobedience, because the offense of disobedience is in one respect, while the offense of obedience is in many respects. God purifies His servant of his offenses through kinds of calamities, so as to lighten his burdens on the Day of Resurrection. Had it not been for His pardon and mercy, he would have perished at the first step."

And from 'Alī - may God be pleased with him -: "This is the most hopeful verse for the believers in the Qur'an, for the Generous One, when He punishes once, does not punish a second time, and when He pardons, does not return to it."

Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers. The passage is short; translate it faithfully.

"And you cannot escape (in the earth)" — meaning: you cannot escape what He has decreed upon you of calamities. (p-257) "And you have no protector (wali) besides Allah," one who takes charge with mercy, "nor any helper (nasir)," one who supports you and repels the punishment from you when it descends upon you.

Here is the translation:

﴿And you cannot escape (Him) on earth﴾, that is: you cannot escape what He has decreed upon you of calamities. (p-257) ﴿And you have no protector (wali) besides Allah﴾, one who takes charge of you with mercy, ﴿nor any helper (nasir)﴾, one who supports you and repels the punishment from you when it befalls you.

﴿And among His signs are the ships﴾, the plural of "jāriyah," which means the ship. "al-Jawārī" in both states (pausing and continuing), according to Makkī, Sahl and Ya‘qūb. Madanī and Abū ‘Amr agreed with them in continuing recitation (waṣl, joining the word to what follows without a pause), ﴿in the sea like mountains﴾, like mountains.

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾, "الرِّياحَ" (al-riyāḥa, the plural), read by Madani (the Medinan reader).

﴿So they remain motionless﴾, steadfast, not moving,

﴿on its back﴾, on the back of the sea,

﴿Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾, patient over His trials, and grateful for His blessings. That is, for every sincere believer, since faith is two halves: half gratitude and half patience. Or: patient in obeying Him, grateful for His favor.

Or He destroys them (ﷻ) for what they have earned, and pardons many (of them).

Here "yubiqhunna" means "yuhlikhunna" (He destroys them), and it is coordinated with "yuskin" (He stills). The meaning is: "If He wills, He stills the wind so that they stand motionless, or He drives it violently so that they drown by its violence,"

"bima kasabu" (for what they have earned), namely the sins,

"wa-ya'fu 'an kathir" (and pardons many), of them, so that He does not requite them for them. Pardon here is in the sense of destruction, in that it is put in the jussive mood just as the destruction is, because the meaning is: "Or if He wills, He destroys some people and saves some people, by way of pardoning them."

{And that He may know} — in the accusative (naṣb), coordinated (ʿaṭf) upon an implied causal clause, its estimated form being: "so that He may take vengeance upon them, and that He may know,"

{those who dispute concerning Our signs} — i.e., in nullifying them and repelling them. {"And He knows"} — read by the Medinans and the Syrian reader (Ibn ʿĀmir), as a resumptive (istiʾnāf) new sentence,

{they have no place of escape} — no refuge from His punishment.

﴿Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment of this worldly life, but what is with Allah, that is, from the reward, is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.﴾

The first "ما" (mā) in the verse has been treated as carrying the meaning of a conditional particle, so the "فاء" (fa') came in its response, unlike the second "ما". It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when he gave away all his wealth in charity, and the people blamed him.

(p-258) ﴿And those who avoid﴾: it is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon "those who believed" (alladhīna āmanū), and so is what follows it,

﴿the grave sins (kabāʾir al-ithm)﴾: i.e., the major sins of this kind. Read as "kabīra al-ithm" (the singular), by ʿAlī and Ḥamza. And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "kabīr al-ithm" is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

﴿and the indecencies (al-fawāḥish)﴾: it has been said that these are things whose ugliness is great, so each is a fāḥisha, such as fornication (zinā).

﴿and when they are angry (wa-idhā mā ghaḍibū)﴾: over matters of their worldly affairs.

﴿they forgive (hum yaghfirūn)﴾: i.e., they are the ones specially singled out for forgiveness in the state of anger. The bringing of "hum" (they), placing it as the subject (mubtadaʾ), and attributing "yaghfirūn" (they forgive) to it, is for this purpose. A similar example is: ﴿they defend themselves (hum yantaṣirūn)﴾ [al-Shūrā: 39].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 38:

﴿Those who have responded to their Lord﴾. It was revealed concerning the Ansar (the Helpers of Madina). Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, called them to believe in Him and to obey Him, so they responded to Him by believing in Him and obeying Him.

﴿And establish the prayer﴾, and they completed the five daily prayers.

﴿And whose affair is [conducted by] consultation among themselves﴾, meaning: they hold consultation, and do not act on an opinion alone until they agree upon it. It is related from al-Hasan: "No people consult together except that they are guided to the best of their affairs." And "al-shura" (consultation) is a verbal noun, like "al-futya" (a legal verdict), meaning "al-tasha'wur" (mutual consultation).

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾, meaning: they give in charity.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 39:

﴿And those who, when tyranny (al-baghy) afflicts them,﴾ — al-Baghy: oppression, wrongdoing.

﴿they defend themselves (yantasiruna).﴾ They take revenge upon those who wronged them. That is, they keep within bounds in the retaliation (al-intisar) with what Allah (Exalted is He) has allowed them, and they do not transgress. They used to dislike that they should humiliate themselves, lest the wicked become emboldened against them. They are praised for retaliation because whoever retaliates and takes his right, and does not exceed the limit of Allah in doing so, and does not commit excess in killing (if he is the guardian of blood), is obedient to Allah, and every obedient person is praiseworthy. Then he explained the limit of retaliation, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 40:

﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾. The first is an evil in reality, while the second is not; it is called "evil" only because it is the requital of evil, or because it harms the one upon whom it descends. And if the first were not an evil, the second would be an evil, because it is harm. The second has become good by way of what it leads to. Or the naming of the second as "evil" is an indication that pardon is recommended (mandub), and the meaning is that when an offence is met, it is obligatory that it be answered with its like, without excess,

﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation﴾, between himself and his adversary, by pardon and overlooking,

﴿his reward is with Allah﴾, a vague promise whose magnitude cannot be measured,

﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾, those who initiate wrongdoing, or those who exceed the limit of retaliation in speech. A caller will call out on the Day of Resurrection: "Whoever has a reward with Allah, let him stand up," and none will stand except the one who pardoned.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 41:

﴿And whoever takes retribution after being wronged﴾: he takes his right after he has been wronged, with the verbal noun (maṣdar) idafa (annexed) to its object (maf'ul), [i.e., the wronging is attributed to the object of the act, not its agent].

﴿Those—against them there is no path﴾: "Ulā'ika" (those) is a pointer referring to the meaning of "man" (whoever), not to its wording.

﴿There is no path against them﴾: [no blame] for the one who punishes in return, nor for the one who rebukes, nor for the one who censures.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 42:

﴿Indeed, the blame (al-sabil) is only against those who wrong people﴾, initiating the wrong against them,

﴿and who transgress in the earth﴾, acting arrogantly in it, exalting themselves, and causing corruption,

﴿without right. For them there is a painful punishment﴾. And he explained al-sabil (the way, here: the path of blame/accountability) as liability to punishment (al-taba'a) and the proof (al-hujja).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 43:

﴿And whoever is patient﴾, over injustice and harm,

﴿and forgives﴾, and does not retaliate,

﴿indeed that﴾, i.e., the patience and the forgiveness from him [the one who exhibits them],

﴿is surely of the steadfast matters﴾, i.e., of the matters to which one is urged, or of what a sensible person should oblige himself to, and not grant himself leniency in abandoning. He omitted the returning pronoun, i.e., "from him" (minhu), because it is understood, just as it is omitted in their saying: "Samn manawan bi-dirham" (ghee is two manwan for a dirham). Abu Sa'id al-Qurashi said: "Patience in the face of hardships is one of the signs of the prophets. Whoever is patient with a hardship that befalls him, and does not lament, Allah (Exalted) bequeaths to him the state of contentment (ridā), which is the most noble of states. And whoever laments over calamities, complains, and Allah (Exalted) leaves him to himself, and then his complaint does not benefit him."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 44:

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him.﴾ That is, there is no one who can guide him after Allah has left him astray, and no one who can shield him from His punishment.

﴿And you see the wrongdoers﴾ on the Day of Resurrection,

﴿when they see the punishment﴾ at the moment they see the punishment. The past tense form is used here to express certainty (tahqiq).

﴿they will say, "Is there any way to return?"﴾ They will ask their Lord to return them to the world so that they may believe in Him.

(p-260) ﴿And you will see them presented before it﴾, upon the Fire, since the punishment indicates it,

﴿humbled﴾, diminished, shrinking within themselves because of what befalls them,

﴿from humiliation, they glance﴾, toward the Fire,

﴿with a furtive glance﴾, weak, stealthy, like the glance of one who is being held (to be executed) looking at the sword.

﴿And those who believed will say: Indeed the losers are those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. "On the Day" is connected to "lost," and the saying of the believers takes place in this world; or it is connected to "will say," meaning: "They will say on the Day of Resurrection, when they see them in that state: ﴿Surely the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾," that is, enduring.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 42, verse 46:

﴿And they will have no allies who could help them against Allah﴾, meaning, from other than His punishment.

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way﴾, meaning, to salvation.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 47:

﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ i.e., answer Him in what He has called you to,

﴿before there comes a Day﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection,

﴿for which there is no turning back from Allah﴾. "Min" (from) is connected to "lā maradd" (no turning back), meaning: Allah will not turn it back after He has decreed it. Or it is connected to "yaʾtiya" (comes), meaning: before there comes from Allah a Day which no one is able to turn back.

﴿You will have no refuge that day, nor will you have any denial﴾. i.e., you will have no escape from the punishment, and you will not be able to deny anything of what you committed, which was recorded in the pages of your deeds. And "al-nakīr" (denial) is "al-inkār" (denial/disavowal).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 48:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾, from faith,

﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, a watcher,

﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾, that is, your only obligation is to convey the message, and you have done so.

﴿And when We let man taste﴾, the intended meaning is the collective (mankind), not the single individual,

﴿a mercy from Us﴾, a blessing, abundance, security, and health,

﴿he rejoices in it﴾, he becomes arrogant because of it.

﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾, a trial, such as sickness, poverty, and the like. The singular form of "rejoices" (faraḥa) is in accordance with the word (lafẓ), while the plural in "befalls them" (tuṣibhum) is in accordance with the meaning (maʿnā).

﴿because of what their hands have sent forth﴾, because of their sins,

﴿then indeed man is ungrateful﴾. He did not say "then indeed he is ungrateful" (fa-innahu kafūr), so as to record that this kind of human being is marked by ingratitude for blessings, as He said: ﴿Indeed, man is a great wrongdoer, a great ingrate﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. Al-kafūr is one who is intensely ungrateful. The meaning is that he remembers the trial, forgets the blessings, and denies them. It has been said that what is meant is ingratitude for blessings, and it has been said that what is meant is disbelief in Allah (Exalted).

﴿Or He pairs them, males and females,﴾ i.e., He joins them together.

﴿and He makes whom He wills barren.﴾ When He mentioned man's tasting of mercy and his being struck by its opposite, He followed this with the fact that dominion belongs to Him (exalted is He), that He apportions blessing and affliction as He wills, and that He grants His servants offspring as He wishes: He singles out some with females, some with males, some with both, and makes some barren. "Al-'aqim" (the barren) is the woman who does not bear children; similarly, a "barren man" (raj­ul 'aqim) is one who cannot father children. He mentioned the females first, before the males, because the context of the speech is that He is the doer of whatever He wills, not whatever man wills; so mentioning females, who are among the things man does not will, was more important, and what is more important must be given precedence. Also, so that the category that the Arabs used to regard as a calamity would come directly after the mention of calamity. When He delayed the males, although they deserve precedence, He made up for their delay by making them definite, because definiteness signifies distinction and renown. Then, after that, He gave both categories their due in precedence and delay, and made clear that the precedence of the females was not due to their superiority, but to another consideration. So He said: "males and females."

It was said: it was revealed concerning the prophets (peace be upon them), when He gave Lot and Shu'ayb females, Abraham males, and Muhammad (ﷺ) males and females, and made Yahya and Isa (peace be upon them both) barren.

﴿Indeed He is All-Knowing﴾ of everything, ﴿All-Powerful﴾, able to do everything.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 51:

﴿And it is not for a human [basharin]﴾, that is, it is not right for any human being,

﴿that Allah should speak to him except by revelation (wahy)﴾, i.e., by inspiration (ilham), as it is narrated: "He breathed it into my heart (nafatha fi ruʿi)," or by a vision in sleep, as the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "The dream of the prophets is revelation (wahy)." And this is like the command to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to sacrifice his son,

﴿or from behind a veil﴾, i.e., he hears speech from Allah, as Musa, peace be upon him, heard it, without the hearer seeing the one who is speaking to him. The intended meaning is not the veil of Allah (exalted is He), because what is possible for bodies of veiling does not apply to Allah (exalted is He); rather, the intended meaning is that the hearer is veiled from seeing [Allah] in this world,

﴿or send a messenger﴾, i.e., He sends an angel,

﴿so that he reveals﴾, i.e., the angel reveals to him, it is said: by revelation, just as revelation was sent to the messengers through the mediation of the angels; or [He sends] a messenger, i.e., a prophet, just as He spoke to the nations of the prophets through their tongues. "Wahyan" and "an yursila" are both verbal nouns (masdar) functioning in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), because "an yursila" has the meaning of "irsalan" (sending). And "min wara'i hijab" is an adverbial phrase (zarf) functioning in the position of a circumstantial clause, like the words of Him: ﴿and upon their sides﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191]. The implied meaning is: "It is not right that He speak to anyone except by revealing, or by causing to hear from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger." It is also permissible that the meaning be: "It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revealing, or by causing him to hear from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger." This is the choice of al-Khalil. "Aw yursilu rasulan fa-yuhiya," with the nominative (raf'), is the reading of Nafi', understood as "or He Himself sends," 

﴿by His permission﴾, the permission of Allah,

﴿what He wills﴾, of the revelation,

﴿Indeed He is Exalted﴾, Dominant, so He cannot be opposed,

﴿Wise﴾, correct in His sayings and His deeds, so He cannot be contested.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 42, verse 52:**

﴿And thus﴾, meaning: as We revealed to the messengers before you, or as We have described to you,

﴿We revealed to you﴾, a revelation of that kind,

﴿a spirit from Our command﴾. He means: what was revealed to him, because people are given life by it in their religion, just as the body is given life by the spirit,

﴿you did not know﴾. The clause is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to the kaf in "ilayka" (to you),

﴿what the Book is﴾, namely the Qur'an,

﴿nor faith﴾, meaning its laws (*shara'i'*), or: nor faith in the Book. For if he did not know that the Book would be sent down to him, he would not have known that Book. It has also been said that faith (*iman*) encompasses many things, some of which are reached by reason ('aql) and some of which are reached by revelation (*sam'*). So by it he means what is reached by revelation and not by reason, and that is what he had no knowledge of until he acquired it through revelation.

﴿But We made it﴾, meaning the Book,

﴿a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed you guide﴾, meaning you call (*latad'u*, "to call"). It was also recited with that reading,

﴿to a straight path﴾, which is Islam.

﴿The path of Allah﴾ is a *badal* (a substitute or appositional noun that restates the preceding word).

﴿He to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: *mulkan* (in the sense of sovereignty, dominion) and *milkan* (in the sense of ownership, possession).

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all affairs return﴾: this is a threat of the Fire and a promise of bliss.
